facts.fact: The Ifakara Health Institute's mid-term review of HSSP V, citing SARA 2023, states that only 10.6% of dispensaries use GOT-HoMIS, which it describes as an electronic medical record system and data aggregation tool; no numerator or denominator is given.
The mid-term review of HSSP V, citing SARA 2023, states that 44.9% of health centres use GOT-HoMIS, the highest proportion of any facility type; no numerator or denominator is given.

The mid-term review's figure of facilities using GOT-HoMIS, from SARA 2023, gives 23.25% of health facilities overall, against 32.1% of district hospitals, 44.9% of health centres and 10.63% of dispensaries; this is a share of all facilities, with no numerator or denominator.

The mid-term review states that more than 3,000 primary health care facilities use GoT-HoMIS as their electronic medical record system; it gives no denominator and no date, so the document's published month is used.
The mid-term review, on SARA 2023, reports GOT-HoMIS in use in 32.1% of district hospitals, 44.9% of health centres and 10.63% of dispensaries.

The mid-term review states that all 28 regional hospitals use Afya eHMS, the Ministry of Health's EMR system for patient-level management, and that zonal and specialised hospitals use a mix of systems that includes it; it gives no date, so the document's published month is used.

Against the HSSP V commitment to expand electronic medical records in all facilities from PHC to national hospital, the mid-term review reports EMR used in all facilities at higher levels and in more than 3,000 PHC facilities; it gives no date, so the document's published month is used.
facts.system: electronic medical record systems (GoT-HoMIS, Afya eHMS, E-Medical, Medipro, Inaya, GIVA)

facts.fact: The mid-term review states that the Ministry of Health developed and launched the Hospital Management System (Afya eHMS) for all regional hospitals, piloted first at Amana Regional Referral Hospital, and plans to replace vendor-dependent systems with unified government-owned ones; no date is given, so the document's published month is used.

The mid-term review names Medipro and E-Medical, EMR systems used in zonal and specialised hospitals, as vendor-dependent systems the Ministry of Health plans to phase out; no date is given, so the document's published month is used.

The mid-term review records that HSSP V commits to expanding electronic medical record systems that exchange information with the national HMIS in all health facilities from PHC to national hospital, and that expanding GOT-HoMIS is a priority for PO-RALG and the Ministry of Health; the Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024 has run out and its 2025-2030 successor was still being developed, with the investment roadmap supported by UNICEF.
facts.system: electronic medical record systems (GoT-HoMIS, Afya eHMS)

facts.fact: The mid-term review records the HSSP V commitment to maintain the HMIS central data warehouse and improve its visualisation tools, reported as met with dashboards, and the Ministry of Health's effort to make DHIS2 the main health information system with EMR data submitted directly into it, full interoperability having been expected by December 2024.

The mid-term review describes the Ministry of Health as making DHIS2 the main health information system, with the Health Information System Program (HISP) supporting it through DHIS2 academies, training, systems development and implementations; no date is given, so the document's published month is used.
